title: 4.2 Complex Solutions of Equations

icans: I can tell how many solutions a polynomial equation has.
I can use the discriminant to describe the solutions of a quadratic equation.
I can find all the complex zeros of a polynomial.

vocab: every _____________ of degree n > 0 has at least one zero in the complex number system
b² − 4ac, the _____________ under the radical in the Quadratic Formula
a _____________ of degree n has exactly n linear factors, f(x) = a(x − c₁)(x − c₂)⋯(x − cₙ)

blocks.p: Graph each one in Desmos. Count the x-intercepts and find b² − 4ac.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Number of solutions: a polynomial equation of degree n has exactly _______________ solutions in the complex numbers (counting repeated ones).

blocks.stem: How many solutions does x³ + 4x = 0 have? Find them.

notes: Discriminant b² − 4ac: positive → two real solutions; zero → one repeated real solution; negative → two _______________.

blocks.stem:
Describe the solutions.
a.  x² + 2x + 5 = 0
b.  4x² − 12x + 9 = 0

notes: Complex Conjugate Zeros: if a + bi (b ≠ 0) is a zero of a polynomial with real coefficients, then _______________ is also a zero.

blocks.stem: 1 + 3i is a zero of f(x) = x⁴ − 3x³ + 6x² + 2x − 60. Find all the zeros.
Write x⁴ − 16 as a product of linear factors.
Find all the zeros of f(x) = x³ − x² + 4x − 4.
